entrypoints.summary: A product stock-check request accepts a URL in the stockApi parameter; the lab instructs interception and modification of that request.

observability.channel: HTTP response or lab interface behavior
negative_controls: The lab states that http://127.0.0.1/ is blocked.
The lab states that http://127.1/admin is blocked before path-character obfuscation.
observability.positive_marker: The lab says the bypass accesses the admin interface and allows deletion of carlos.

preconditions: The attacker can submit or intercept a product stock-check request containing the stockApi parameter.
The stock-check feature performs a server-side fetch and the lab's weak anti-SSRF filters are present.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: HTTP URL with abbreviated loopback IPv4 address.
trigger_steps.summary: Replace stockApi with the alternate loopback form http://127.1/ to bypass the block on the literal 127.0.0.1 form.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Loopback URL with an admin path containing a double-encoded character.
trigger_steps.summary: Use the 127.1 admin path while double-URL-encoding the a character as %2561 to bypass the literal admin-path block.
Use the reached admin interface to delete the specified user.

capabilities.concept: Bypass blacklist URL filtering through alternate loopback notation and double URL encoding
Server-side request to loopback admin interface

mitigations.concept: Canonicalized allowlist-based authorization of server-side URL destinations

relation_candidates.dst: Bypass blacklist URL filtering through alternate loopback notation and double URL encoding
relation_candidates.rationale: The stockApi parameter is modified to use the alternate 127.1 loopback form and a double-encoded path character, bypassing the described blocks.

relation_candidates.dst: Server-side request to loopback admin interface
relation_candidates.rationale: The documented bypass sequence reaches the admin interface after the filter blocks literal loopback and admin forms.
relation_candidates.src: Bypass blacklist URL filtering through alternate loopback notation and double URL encoding

relation_candidates.rationale: The lab specifies accessing the internal admin interface and deleting carlos as the successful action.
relation_candidates.src: Server-side request to loopback admin interface

relation_candidates.dst: Canonicalized allowlist-based authorization of server-side URL destinations
relation_candidates.rationale: A canonicalized destination authorization policy is an inferred mitigation that would prevent alternate textual forms from authorizing an unintended loopback destination; no patch is supplied.
relation_candidates.src: Server-side request to loopback admin interface

impact.affected_asset: Internal admin interface and the carlos user account.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause the application to make an HTTP request to an unintended loopback destination and invoke the shown admin action.
impact.security_effect: Unauthorized access to an internal administrative interface and deletion of an account in the lab.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker can replace the stockApi URL in the stock-check request with a chosen HTTP URL.

The lab's blacklist-based defenses block the literal loopback form http://127.0.0.1/ but permit the alternate loopback representation http://127.1/; they also block the literal /admin path but can be bypassed by double-URL-encoding the character a as %2561.
The server-side stock-check feature fetches a user-supplied URL and, after the bypass, can be directed to the loopback admin interface at the equivalent 127.1/admin destination.
The lab states that access to the internal admin interface enables deletion of the user carlos, demonstrating an unauthorized administrative action through the server-side request.

failure.operation: Server-side retrieval of the attacker-controlled stockApi URL at an internal loopback/admin destination.

primary_invariant.statement: The stock-check fetch must not be usable to reach the loopback admin interface or other unintended internal destinations.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The URL filter relies on blocked textual representations that do not account for an alternate loopback address form and a double-decoded path character.

quality.review_notes: This is a PortSwigger training-lab writeup, not a project-specific vulnerability report or inspected implementation. The source supplies a request-modification sequence and stated observables, but no captured execution result, source code, version scope, or remediation patch. The remediation wording is an inferred security condition based on the documented bypass, not an evidenced patch.

remediation.invariant_restored: A stock-check URL is accepted only when its canonicalized destination is authorized and cannot resolve or normalize to the loopback admin interface.
mitigation_classes: Canonicalize and authorize URL destinations before server-side fetches
Avoid blacklist-only matching of host and path text

target.component: stock check feature and its stockApi URL input
target.project_or_package: PortSwigger Web Security Academy SSRF blacklist-filter lab

oracle.expected_negative: The literal stockApi values http://127.0.0.1/ and http://127.1/admin are reported as blocked in the lab instructions.
oracle.expected_positive: A modified stockApi URL using 127.1 and a double-encoded a in the admin path reaches the lab admin interface, permitting the stated deletion action.
